categories.title: Governance and emergency authority
categories.approved_portion: Only bonded stake gives voting power. Liquid DGT gives zero. Count each owner stake once; do not add validator aggregate stake. An immutable finalized eligible-bond snapshot fixes each proposal's weights and quorum denominator. Each registered account with effective bonded DGT controls its own vote, including validator and delegator bonds. A proposer must be a registered account with positive effective bonded DGT at the finalized parent. Validators have no special vote; signed vote delegation and proposal cancellation are disabled in governance v1. Abstentions count for quorum but not approval or veto. Required weights round up with exact basis-point arithmetic. DGT deposits are refundable escrow at terminal status; no burn or sweep authority. An explicit deposit stage precedes voting; a below-minimum proposal rejects and refunds. Execution requires an explicit finalized-height timelock and an action fixed before voting. The approved ordinary-v3 engineering profile preserves v2 bytes, carries exactly one governance action without mixed ordinary actions, and requires candidate-bound activation; it does not select action classes, fees, or production values.

Production activation (P01, 30 September 2026): validators allow only local owner-only Unix sockets; the engine is checked at startup and then held by kernel limits without periodic pauses; one IP per node with static 1:1 NAT for public sentries; a published partial mesh within 64 pins. Supervisor production mode (P01, 1 October 2026): the engine, application, bridge and HTTP adapter are observed once at startup and then held by kernel limits; readiness waits for catch-up up to a per-host budget. Host settings (P01, 2 October 2026): supervisor process limits, a 1 s pause-free monitor, a six-hour catch-up budget, the retained block window everywhere with archive only on designated archive nodes, the adapter at its compiled ceilings, and the emergency verifier bounds. Host setup (P01, 6 October 2026): Ubuntu 24.04 LTS on every host; each host's public IPv4 on its own interface with no NAT, replacing the static 1:1 NAT above; node keys made offline and delivered in digest-checked host bundles with the keys sealed under a passphrase (AES-256); the service account dytallix (41001) and the /opt, /etc and /var/lib/dytallix layout with one unit (host setup v1). Host values (P01, 6 October 2026): 6 GiB memory, 4,096 tasks and 65,536 open files per host; ports 26656, 26670 and 8080; root-owned code; the catalog, observation and root helper bounds; 30-second root and emergency verifier timeouts (launch/hosts/SETUP_VALUES.json). Host sealing (P01, 6 October 2026): each host's node keys sealed by dytallix-root-sign seal under the host's own 256-bit seal code (AES-256-GCM, key from SHAKE256), printed once as a checked paper line, written twice and kept with two different kits' papers. Release switch (P01, 6 October 2026): a host stages a new release beside the running one from its new bundle, keeping the node home and keys, and switches the unit to it when the old release stops at activation; the previous release stays until the next stage. Supervisor root preflight (P01, 7 October 2026): the production supervisor never runs the root helper; it selects the release from the pinned inputs and the application verifies the root signatures before opening state.

launch_profile.summary: One person, the founder, runs the network and holds its controls at launch: one validator on three hosts, every root key in five key kits, 100% of DGT in public bucket accounts, a public review instead of an independent human audit, and best-effort operations.
